(for Res. No.4) Coram:
The Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Biraja Prasanna Satapathy Order Order No.
05.12.2025
15. 1.
This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual/Physical) Mode.

2. Heard learned counsel appearing for the parties.
3.

Placing reliance on the provisions contained under Section 66(3)(h) of the old Motor Vehicle Act,
learned counsel appearing for the Respondent-University contended that the University is not liable to pay the compensation so assessed by the Tribunal.
4. Mr. P.K. Mahali, learned counsel appearing for the Appellant on the other hand contended that such provision contained under Section 66(3)(h) has already been omitted w.e.f 11.08.2000.

5. At this point of time, learned counsel appearing for the Respondent-University contended that in view of the // 2 // provisions contained under Section 66(3)(a) of the Act, the Respondent-University is also otherwise not liable to pay the compensation, as there was no requirement to have a permit.

6. Considering the submission made by Mr. N.R. Routray, learned counsel appearing for Respondent No.4, he is directed to file an affidavit that the University was not charging any fees from the students by utilizing the bus in question.

This Court also requires assistance from Mr. P.K. Behera, learned Standing Counsel for Transport Deptt. to sort out the issue raised in the present I.A.

Learned counsel appearing for the appellant is directed to provide a copy of the appeal memo along with the I.A to Mr. P Behera,
learned Standing Counsel for the Transport Deptt. by 10.12.2025.
7.
List this matter in the week commencing 12.01.2026.
Office is directed to indicate the name of Mr. P.Behera, learned Standing Counsel in the cause list.
